# Adjudication Task — Chapter 497

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃497화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|한 식경(食頃).
  6|
  7|그것이 내가 버틸 수 있는 최대한의 시간이었다. 목덜미로부터 느껴지는 검날의 서늘한 감촉에, 나는 작게 중얼거렸다.
  8|
  9|“거지 같네, 진짜.”
 10|
 11|스윽.
 12|
 13|따끔한 통증과 함께 핏물이 목덜미를 타고 미끄러진다. 의도가 뻔히 보이는 행동에 절로 한숨이 흘러나온다.
 14|
 15|“졌습니다. 그만하시죠.”
 16|
 17|“틀렸다. 다시.”
 18|
 19|싸우는 도중에는 들을 수 없었던 건조한 목소리. 그리고 나는 목소리의 주인이 원하는 대답을 이미 알고 있었다.
 20|
 21|“……죽었습니다. 됐어요?”
 22|
 23|천천히 목덜미를 파고들던 검날이 우뚝 멈춘다. 이내 차가운 날붙이의 감촉이 사라지는 것을 느낀 나는 목을 짚어 지혈한 뒤 돌아섰다.
 24|
 25|어느새 삼 장 밖의 바위에 앉아 있는 한 사람이 보였다.
 26|
 27|“네가 몇 번째 죽었는지는 알고 있나?”
 28|
 29|“열두 번이요.”
 30|
 31|사지 근맥이 잘려 죽은 경우가 다섯 번, 사혈(死穴)을 점혈 당하여 죽은 것이 세 번. 심장이 관통당한 것 역시 세 번. 그리고 조금 전에는 목이 베였다.
 32|
 33|실제로 죽진 않았지만, 죽은 거나 마찬가지다. 옷소매로 목에 묻은 끈적한 핏물을 닦아 낸 나는 문경을 바라보았다.
 34|
 35|“다음번에는 다를 겁니다.”
 36|
 37|“열한 번째 듣는 말이로군.”
 38|
 39|“이번엔 확실해요.”
 40|
 41|“그건 열두 번째고.”
 42|
 43|“…….”
 44|
 45|기억력 보소. 할 말을 잃어버린 나를 향해 문경이 물었다.
 46|
 47|“네놈이 왜 죽었는지 알고 있나?”
 48|
 49|싸움은 언제나 결과를 남기고, 결과는 항상 생각을 낳는다.
 50|
 51|말없이 머릿속으로 문경과의 싸움을 떠올리던 내가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
 52|
 53|“살수처럼 싸워서?”
 54|
 55|“역시 아무것도 모르는…… 흠.”
 56|
 57|나와 거의 동시에 말문을 열었던 문경이 말꼬리를 흐렸다.
 58|
 59|“틀렸습니까?”
 60|
 61|“계속해 봐라.”
 62|
 63|“정확히 언제부터인지는 모르겠는데, 따라 하게 되더라고요. 보여 주시는 움직임이나 그런 것들을.”
 64|
 65|처음에는 독 장아찌가 될 정도로 당하고 나니 주위의 모든 것에 주의하게 됐고, 그 후부터는 문경의 움직임을 조금씩 베끼기 시작했다.
 66|
 67|그렇게 하루에 두세 번씩 비무를 치르다 보니 점점 눈과 몸에 익어 갔다.
 68|
 69|하지만…….
 70|
 71|“그게 패착이었어요.”
 72|
 73|“어째서지?”
 74|
 75|“원래 새 신발을 신으면 발뒤꿈치가 까지는 법이죠. 그 신발이 발 크기보다 작으면 두말할 것도 없고.”
 76|
 77|“더 자세히.”
 78|
 79|“되지도 않는 어설픈 흉내는 집어치우고, 제 방식대로 싸웠어야 했습니다. 상대가 살성일 경우에는 더더욱.”
 80|
 81|“…….”
 82|
 83|한동안 말없이 나를 물끄러미 응시하던 문경이 한마디를 툭 내뱉었다.
 84|
 85|“아주 천치는 아니로군.”
 86|
 87|“오, 방금 그거 설마 칭찬하신 겁니까?”
 88|
 89|“이제 겨우 기본이라는 뜻이다.”
 90|
 91|“그러니까요. 칭찬 감사합니다.”
 92|
 93|문경이 미간을 찡그렸다.
 94|
 95|“네놈은 귓구멍이 막혔느냐?”
 96|
 97|“아뇨. 뚫렸는데요?”
 98|
 99|“……사람을 열 받게 하는 재주가 있군.”
100|
101|“결국 기본이 됐다는 거니까 칭찬 맞지 않습니까. 왜 이렇게 솔직하지 못하세요? 혹시 사춘기십니까?”
102|
103|“아니라니까!”
104|
105|“아니, 왜 갑자기 소리를 그렇게.”
106|
107|“내가 언제! 아니라고!”
108|
109|“……생각해 보니 그런 것도 같네요.”
110|
111|아니긴 뭐가 아니야.
112|
113|하지만 말대꾸 한 번만 더 했다가는 목이 날아갈 기세다.
114|
115|버럭 소리를 지른 문경은 언제 그랬냐는 듯 평온하면서도 건조한 어조로 돌아왔다.
116|
117|“기본은 말 그대로 기본일 뿐이다. 지금까지 그런 놈들은 네 녀석 말고도 여럿 있었지.”
118|
119|그런 놈들?
120|
121|나는 설마 하는 마음으로 입을 열었다.
122|
123|“혹시 다른 제자가 있습니까?”
124|
125|“당연히 있지. 사천에서 만나지 않았더냐.”
126|
127|“동 노인 말고요. 무슨 뜻인지 뻔히 아시면서 다른 소리 하시네.”
128|
129|“…….”
130|
131|침묵은 곧 긍정. 숨겨진 살성의 제자가 있다고 생각하자 호기심이 고개를 치켜들었다.
132|
133|“누구, 누굽니까? 지금도 계속 연락 주고받고 그래요? 스승의 날에 다 같이 밥도 같이 먹고?”
134|
135|“내가 대답해 줄 이유는 없지. 그리고 스승의 날이라니, 무슨 개소리냐?”
136|
137|“까탈스럽게 구시긴.”
138|
139|“……날이 갈수록 언행이 방자해지는군. 목숨이 다섯 개쯤 되나?”
140|
141|“지금까지 열두 번 죽고 되살아난 것으로 봐서는 열세 개 정도는 되는 것 같은데요. 그래서 진짜 안 알려 주실 겁니까?”
142|
143|나를 뚫어져라 노려보던 문경이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
144|
145|“알려 주지. 단, 조건이 있다.”
146|
147|살성의 제시하는 조건이라. 나는 자신감 넘치는 태도로 입을 열었다.
148|
149|“슬슬 밥 먹을 시간이네요. 이만 가 보겠습니다.”
150|
151|“분명 먹고 온 것으로 기억하는데.”
152|
153|“제가 하루에 다섯 끼는 먹어서요.”
154|
155|“그래도 듣고 가지. 상당히 궁금해하는 것 같던데.”
156|
157|“각자 인생이 있고 감추고 싶은 비밀이 있는 법인데, 그걸 뭐 하러 캐묻겠습니까. 그럼 전 이만.”
158|
159|“딱 서라. 목 날아가기 싫으면.”
160|
161|“…….”
162|
163|시벌, 괜히 물어봤다.
164|
165|나는 똥줄이 타들어 가는 것을 느끼며 반쯤 돌린 신형을 원위치했다.
166|
167|그래, 기왕 이렇게 된 거 이야기나 듣자.
168|
169|“그래서, 정말 또 다른 제자들이 있는 겁니까?”
170|
171|“제자는 아니지만, 가르침을 내린 놈들이라면 여럿 있었다.”
172|
173|“이제는 없다는 뜻으로 들리네요.”
174|
175|“실로 오랜 세월이 흘렀으니까. 지금까지 살아남았을 리 없지.”
176|
177|“혹시 그분들께서 몸담으셨던 분야가……?”
178|
179|“살수였다. 나와 함께 살천문(殺天門)에 속해 있었던.”
180|
181|살천문이라. 듣기만 해도 피비린내 솔솔 나는 이름이다.
182|
183|‘이 인간, 사문도 있었구나.’
184|
185|생각해 보면 당연한 일이었다. 제아무리 문경이라 할지라도 처음부터 살수로 태어나지는 않았을 테니까.
186|
187|‘그래도 살성이 소속된 문파였다면 상당히 알려진 이름일 텐데.’
188|
189|지금까지의 기억을 샅샅이 뒤져 봐도, 살천문이라는 세 글자는 생소하다.
190|
191|바로 그때, 내 의문을 알아차린 것처럼 문경이 입술을 뗐다.
192|
193|“소용없다. 이미 오래전 사라진 곳이니.”
194|
195|문파가 사라진다면 그건 한 가지 경우뿐이다.
196|
197|나는 문경의 눈치를 살피며 조심스럽게 한 단어를 입에 올렸다.
198|
199|“멸문(滅門)?”
200|
201|“그래.”
202|
203|“도대체 어쩌다가? 아니, 그전에 본인이 문주 아니셨어요?”
204|
205|“잘못된 길을 택했고, 그에 대한 대가를 치렀지. 해 줄 말은 그뿐이다.”
206|
207|말을 끝마친 문경이 몸을 일으켰다. 그의 손에는 어느새 소검이 시퍼런 예기를 뿜어내고 있었다.
208|
209|“자. 이제 값을 치를 시간이로군.”
210|
211|“예?”
212|
213|“내 일검(一劍)을 피해 보아라. 그게 조건이다.”
214|
215|보통은 도대체 그걸 어떻게 피해, 라고 생각하겠지만 내 입장에서는 충분히 해 볼 만하다.
216|
217|천하의 살성을 상대로, 그것도 어설픈 살수 흉내를 내면서 한 식경을 버텼는데 일검쯤이야.
218|
219|“이거 피하면, 나중에 또 이야기 들려주실 겁니까?”
220|
221|“물론.”
222|
223|“좋습니다, 까짓거.”
224|
225|문경이 한마디를 덧붙였다.
226|
227|“단, 눈을 감아라.”
228|
229|“시발 거. 장난하십니까?”
230|
231|“그렇다면 죽겠군. 열세 번째가 아니라 처음이자 마지막으로.”
232|
233|말이 끝나기도 전에 문경의 소매가 펄럭였다.
234|
235|지금까지의 경험으로 익숙해진 나는 본능적으로 고개를 틀었지만, 날아온 것은 암기가 아닌 또 다른 무언가였다.
236|
237|‘저건.’
238|
239|안력(眼力)을 극도로 끌어올려야 볼 수 있을 만큼 미세한 크기의 가루들.
240|
241|때마침 내 쪽을 향해 불어오던 바람에 실려 날아온 가루가 공기에 닿는 바로 그 순간.
242|
243|화악!
244|
245|어둠이 세상을 집어삼켰다.
246|
247|아니, 아니다. 어둠이 집어삼킨 것은 세상이 아닌 바로 나였다.
248|
249|삐빅.
250|
251|
252|
253|- [실명산]에 중독되셨습니다!
254|
255|- 일시적으로 시력을 상실합니다!
256|
257|- 빠른 해독이 필요합니다! 해독이 오래 지체되면 영구적인 손상이 일어날 수 있습니다!
258|
259|
260|
261|귓가를 파고드는 시스템 알림과 함께 전신의 털이 곤두섰다.
262|
263|실명산? 독 따위는 상관없다. 아직 만독지환을 착용한 상태니까.
264|
265|문제는 만독지환이 실명산을 해독하는 속도보다, 아무것도 보이지 않는 어둠 너머에서 다가오는 문경의 일검이 훨씬 더 빠르다는 것이다.
266|
267|스으윽.
268|
269|아무것도 보이지 않는다. 그러나 분명하게 느낄 수 있었다.
270|
271|마치 누군가 정지 버튼을 누른 것처럼 느리게 흐르는 세상 속에서, 바람을 지우며 다가오는 살검(殺劍)을.
272|
273|‘이건.’
274|
275|고금제일의 살수가 펼친 한 수.
276|
277|지금까지 느껴 본 적 없는, 몸서리칠 만큼 은밀하고 소름 끼치는 살기가 느껴진다.
278|
279|나는 온통 암흑으로 가득한 세상을 멍하니 바라보았다.
280|
281|그리고 아무것도 보이지 않는 그 숨 막히는 공간 속에서, 내 안의 모든 감각이 깨어남을 느꼈다.
282|
283|서걱!
284|
285|
286|
287|* * *
288|
289|
290|
291|무당파, 제갈세가. 그리고 개방.
292|
293|기밀을 위해 믿을 만한 정예들만을 선별했다고는 하나, 그들의 면면과 숫자는 누구도 무시할 수 없을 정도였다.
294|
295|그리고 기백 명이 넘는 명문 대파의 무림인들 사이에서 소년 의생의 모습은 어디에서나 눈에 띌 수밖에 없었다.
296|
297|“오, 너로구나. 지금 나오는 길이냐?”
298|
299|“진 공자님을 뵙고 오는 길입니다.”
300|
301|“근래 들어 더욱 자주 들르는 것 같은데?”
302|
303|“예. 요즘 수련을 워낙 거칠게 하시는 통에, 자꾸 다치셔서요.”
304|
305|“허어. 그렇구나. 진 대협도 참 대단하시지. 나이도 따지면 내 아들놈보다도 어린데, 지금의 경지에 만족하지 않고 끊임없이 노력하시는 모습이…….”
306|
307|“대단한 고수이신가 봐요. 저야 무림에 관한 일은 영 문외한이라.”
308|
309|소년 의생, 문경의 순진무구한 한마디에 경계를 서고 있던 제갈세가의 무인이 피식 웃었다.
310|
311|아무리 심심했기로서니 배운 것이라고는 의술밖에 없는 어린아이를 붙잡고 귀찮게 했다는 생각에서였다.
312|
313|“대단하시지. 그렇고말고. 너도 언젠가 알게 될 게다.”
314|
315|“으음. 그런가요?”
316|
317|“무림에 연관이 없다면 잘 모를 수도 있단다. 어쨌건 이제 오늘 수련은 마무리된 게냐?”
318|
319|아무것도 모르는 양, 고개를 갸우뚱거리던 문경이 대답했다.
320|
321|“아뇨. 앞으로 두 시진 동안은 아무도 접근하지 말라고 하셨어요.”
322|
323|“알겠다. 다른 사람도 아니고 진 대협의 수련을 방해할 수는 없지. 다음 근무자들에게도 전달하도록 하마.”
324|
325|“네. 그럼 고생하세요.”
326|

But no matter how thoroughly I searched my memory, the name Salcheonmun meant nothing to me.

[P94]
As if he’d read my mind, Mungyeong spoke.

[P95]
“No use trying to remember it. The sect vanished long ago.”

[P96]
There was only one way for a sect to vanish. Watching his expression, I carefully said one word.

[P97]
“Annihilated?”

[P98]
“Yes.”

[P99]
“How did that happen? Wait, weren’t you the Sect Leader?”

[P100]
“They chose the wrong path and paid the price. That’s all I’ll say.”

[P101]
Mungyeong rose. At some point, a short sword had appeared in his hand, its keen edge gleaming blue.

[P102]
“Now it’s time for you to pay.”

[P103]
“Excuse me?”

[P104]
“Dodge one sword stroke. That’s the condition.”

[P105]
Most people would think, *How the hell am I supposed to dodge that?* But I had a decent shot.

[P106]
I’d lasted half an hour against the Slaughter Saint while doing a lousy imitation of an assassin. Surely I could dodge one stroke.

[P107]
“If I do, will you tell me more later?”

[P108]
“Of course.”

[P109]
“Fine. I can do that.”

[P110]
Mungyeong added, “Close your eyes.”

[P111]
“Fuck. Are you kidding me?”

[P112]
“Then you’ll die. Not for the thirteenth time, but for the first and last.”

[P113]
Before he’d finished speaking, Mungyeong’s sleeve fluttered.

[P114]
By now, I was used to his attacks. I instinctively turned my head, but what came flying toward me wasn’t a hidden weapon. It was something else.

[P115]
*That’s…*

[P116]
A powder so fine I could barely make it out even when I strained my eyes to their limit.

[P117]
It rode the wind blowing toward me. The instant the powder touched the air—

[P118]
Whoosh!

[P119]
Darkness swallowed the world.

[P120]
No. That wasn’t right.

[P121]
The darkness hadn’t swallowed the world. It had swallowed me.

[P122]
Beep.

[P123]
> **System**
>
> You have been poisoned by **Blindness Powder**!
>
> You temporarily lose your eyesight!
>
> Rapid **Detoxification** is required! If Detoxification is delayed too long, permanent damage may occur!

[P124]
Every hair on my body stood on end as the System alert sounded in my ears.

[P125]
Blindness Powder? The poison itself didn’t matter. I was still wearing the Myriad-Poison Ring.

[P126]
The problem was that Mungyeong’s sword was coming through the darkness far faster than the ring could detoxify the Blindness Powder.

[P127]
Ssshhk.

[P128]
I couldn’t see a thing. But I could feel it clearly.

[P129]
In a world moving so slowly it felt as though someone had pressed pause, a killing sword approached, erasing the wind in its path.

[P130]
*This is…*

[P131]
A move from the greatest assassin of all time.

[P132]
I felt a killing intent unlike anything I’d ever encountered—so stealthy and chilling that I shuddered.

[P133]
I stared blankly into the darkness.

[P134]
And in that suffocating space where I could see nothing, I felt every sense I had awaken.

[P135]
Slash!

[P136]
* * *

[P137]
Wudang, the Zhuge Clan, and the Beggars’ Sect.

[P138]
They had chosen only trustworthy elites to preserve secrecy, but no one could ignore either the standing or the number of those gathered.

[P139]
Among the hundreds of martial artists from those renowned sects, a young medical apprentice was bound to stand out wherever he went.

[P140]
“Oh, it’s you. Just coming out?”

[P141]
“I’ve just been to see Young Master Jin.”

[P142]
“You seem to visit him more often these days.”

[P143]
“Yes. His training has been so rough lately that he keeps getting hurt.”

[P144]
“Good heavens. Great Hero Jin really is remarkable. He’s younger than my son, but he isn’t content with his current realm. He just keeps working…”

[P145]
“He must be an incredible master. I don’t know much about Murim myself.”

[P146]
The Zhuge martial artist standing guard let out a short laugh at the young medical apprentice’s innocent remark. Boredom had led him to bother a child who’d learned nothing but medicine, and now he felt a little guilty.

[P147]
“He is. You’ll understand someday.”

[P148]
“Hmm. Will I?”

[P149]
“If you’re not involved in Murim, you might not know. Anyway, is his training over for today?”

[P150]
Mungyeong tilted his head as though he knew nothing.

[P151]
“No. He said no one should come near him for the next two shichen.”

[P152]
“Understood. We can’t interrupt Great Hero Jin’s training. I’ll tell the guards on the next shift.”

[P153]
“Thank you. Take care.”

[P154]
Mungyeong bowed politely and was about to leave when the martial artist spoke again.

[P155]
“My, his training must be rougher than I thought.”

[P156]
“Sorry?”

[P157]
“The blood on your sleeve. Was Great Hero Jin badly hurt?”

[P158]
The guard’s follow-up question never reached Mungyeong. He looked down at the bloodstain on his sleeve and murmured, “The basics…?”

[P159]
“Hmm?”

[P160]
“Oh, it’s nothing. Young Master Jin is fine, so don’t worry.”

[P161]
“Ah. Good. All right.”

[P162]
Mungyeong walked away, leaving the uneasy-looking guard behind.

[P163]
Several familiar faces greeted him as he passed, but the young medical apprentice had only one person on his mind.

[P164]
*Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung…*

[P165]
He’d thought it couldn’t happen. Yet the boy really had dodged that final sword stroke.

[P166]
The results of the past several days of testing, and of today, had exceeded Mungyeong’s expectations. No, they had exceeded anything he’d imagined.

[P167]
*So this can happen.*

[P168]
Everything he’d told Jin Taekyung was true.

[P169]
He had once taught people he could fairly call Disciples, and all of them had mastered the “basics.”

[P170]
But there was one thing he hadn’t mentioned: how long that had taken.

[P171]
*The fastest of them took a little over a year, if I remember right.*

[P172]
Jin Taekyung had done it in only seven days and nights.

[P173]
No one else came close.

[P174]
Mungyeong didn’t know whether it was because of the boy’s Heavenly Martial Physique or because he was a Supreme Peak master. Whatever the reason, there was something special about Jin Taekyung himself.

[P175]
“Even so… I never expected this much.”

[P176]
He murmured too softly for anyone to hear and rolled up his sleeve.

[P177]
The skin had been cut by something sharp, and beads of blood had formed along the wound. Looking at it, Mungyeong had a sudden thought.

[P178]
*Now I understand how the Fire King feels.*

[P179]
But Mungyeong didn’t realize a faint smile had appeared on his face.

[P180]

[P181]
[^2]: *Salcheonmun* is the name of the now-vanished assassin sect; it literally means “Slaughter Heaven Sect.”

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

“I should’ve quit the clumsy imitation and fought my own way. Especially against the Slaughter Saint.”

[P40]
“……”

[P41]
Mungyeong stared at me for a while, then tossed out a single remark.

[P42]
“You’re not a complete idiot.”

[P43]
“Oh, was that a compliment?”

[P44]
“It means you’ve only just mastered the basics.”

[P45]
“Exactly. Thank you for the compliment.”

[P46]
Mungyeong frowned.

[P47]
“Are your ears plugged?”

[P48]
“Nope. They work fine.”

[P49]
“…You have a gift for getting on people’s nerves.”

[P50]
“If I’ve mastered the basics, it was a compliment. Why can’t you just admit it? Are you going through puberty?”

[P51]
“I said I’m not!”

[P52]
“Why are you shouting all of a sudden?”

[P53]
“When did I— I said I’m not!”

[P54]
“…Now that I think about it, maybe you are.”

[P55]
*Not going through puberty, my ass.*

[P56]
But if I talked back one more time, my head looked liable to fly off.

[P57]
After that outburst, Mungyeong returned to his usual calm, dry tone as though nothing had happened.

[P58]
“The basics are just that: the basics. There have been plenty of others like you.”

[P59]
*Others like me?*

[P60]
I ventured a question.

[P61]
“Do you have other Disciples?”

[P62]
“Of course. You met one in Sichuan.”

[P63]
“Other than Old Man Dong. You know what I mean. Don’t change the subject.”

[P64]
“……”

[P65]
Silence was as good as an admission. The thought of the Slaughter Saint’s hidden Disciples made me curious.

[P66]
“Who? Who are they? Do you still keep in touch? Do you all get together for a meal on Teacher’s Day[^1]?”

[P67]
“I have no reason to tell you. And what the hell is Teacher’s Day?”

[P68]
“You’re awfully difficult.”

[P69]
“…You grow more insolent by the day. Do you have five lives or something?”

[P70]
“Considering I’ve died and come back twelve times, I’d say I have about thirteen. So you’re really not going to tell me?”

[P71]
Mungyeong stared at me, then spoke abruptly.

[P72]
“I’ll tell you. On one condition.”

[P73]
A condition from the Slaughter Saint. I answered with complete confidence.

[P74]
“It’s about time to eat. I’ll be going now.”

[P75]
“I distinctly remember you eating before you came.”

[P76]
“I eat five meals a day.”

[P77]
“Stay and hear the condition. You seemed quite curious.”

[P78]
“Everyone has a life of their own and secrets they’d rather keep. Who am I to pry? Anyway, I’ll be off.”

[P79]
“Stop right there if you want to keep your head.”

[P80]
“……”

[P81]
*Fuck. I shouldn’t have asked.*

[P82]
My stomach knotted with panic as I turned back around. Fine. Since I was stuck here, I might as well hear the story.

[P83]
“So you really have other Disciples?”

[P84]
“Not Disciples. But I did teach several people.”

[P85]
“That sounds like you’re saying they’re gone.”

[P86]
“It’s been a very long time. They couldn’t possibly still be alive.”

[P87]
“Were they, by any chance, in the same line of work as…?”

[P88]
“They were assassins. They belonged to Salcheonmun with me.”[^2]

[P89]
*Salcheonmun.* The name alone sounded bloody.

[P90]
*So he belonged to a sect, too.*

[P91]
It made sense. Mungyeong hadn’t been born an assassin.

[P92]
*Still, a sect the Slaughter Saint belonged to should be fairly well known.*

[P93]
But no matter how thoroughly I searched my memory, the name Salcheonmun meant nothing to me.

[P94]
As if he’d read my mind, Mungyeong spoke.

[P95]
“No use trying to remember it. The sect vanished long ago.”

[P96]
There was only one way for a sect to vanish. Watching his expression, I carefully said one word.

[P97]
“Annihilated?”

[P98]
“Yes.”

[P99]
“How did that happen? Wait, weren’t you the Sect Leader?”

[P100]
“They chose the wrong path and paid the price. That’s all I’ll say.”

[P101]
Mungyeong rose. At some point, a short sword had appeared in his hand, its keen edge gleaming blue.

[P102]
“Now it’s time for you to pay.”

[P103]
“Excuse me?”

[P104]
“Dodge one sword stroke. That’s the condition.”

[P105]
Most people would think, *How the hell am I supposed to dodge that?* But I had a decent shot.

[P106]
I’d lasted half an hour against the Slaughter Saint while doing a lousy imitation of an assassin. Surely I could dodge one stroke.

[P107]
“If I do, will you tell me more later?”

[P108]
“Of course.”

[P109]
“Fine. I can do that.”

[P110]
Mungyeong added, “Close your eyes.”

[P111]
“Fuck. Are you kidding me?”

[P112]
“Then you’ll die. Not for the thirteenth time, but for the first and last.”

[P113]
Before he’d finished speaking, Mungyeong’s sleeve fluttered.

[P114]
By now, I was used to his attacks. I instinctively turned my head, but what came flying toward me wasn’t a hidden weapon. It was something else.

[P115]
*That’s…*

[P116]
A powder so fine I could barely make it out even when I strained my eyes to their limit.

[P117]
It rode the wind blowing toward me. The instant the powder touched the air—

[P118]
Whoosh!

[P119]
Darkness swallowed the world.

[P120]
No. That wasn’t right.

[P121]
The darkness hadn’t swallowed the world. It had swallowed me.

[P122]
Beep.

[P123]
> **System**
>
> You have been poisoned by **Blindness Powder**!
>
> You temporarily lose your eyesight!
>
> Rapid **Detoxification** is required! If Detoxification is delayed too long, permanent damage may occur!

[P124]
Every hair on my body stood on end as the System alert sounded in my ears.

[P125]
Blindness Powder? The poison itself didn’t matter. I was still wearing the Myriad-Poison Ring.

[P126]
The problem was that Mungyeong’s sword was coming through the darkness far faster than the ring could detoxify the Blindness Powder.

[P127]
Ssshhk.

[P128]
I couldn’t see a thing. But I could feel it clearly.

[P129]
In a world moving so slowly it felt as though someone had pressed pause, a killing sword approached, erasing the wind in its path.

[P130]
*This is…*

[P131]
A move from the greatest assassin of all time.

[P132]
I felt a killing intent unlike anything I’d ever encountered—so stealthy and chilling that I shuddered.

[P133]
I stared blankly into the darkness.

[P134]
And in that suffocating space where I could see nothing, I felt every sense I had awaken.

[P135]
Slash!

[P136]
* * *

[P137]
Wudang, the Zhuge Clan, and the Beggars’ Sect.

[P138]
They had chosen only trustworthy elites to preserve secrecy, but no one could ignore either the standing or the number of those gathered.

[P139]
Among the hundreds of martial artists from those renowned sects, a young medical apprentice was bound to stand out wherever he went.

[P140]
“Oh, it’s you. Just coming out?”

[P141]
“I’ve just been to see Young Master Jin.”

[P142]
“You seem to visit him more often these days.”

[P143]
“Yes. His training has been so rough lately that he keeps getting hurt.”

[P144]
“Good heavens. Great Hero Jin really is remarkable. He’s younger than my son, but he isn’t content with his current realm. He just keeps working…”

[P145]
“He must be an incredible master. I don’t know much about Murim myself.”

[P146]
The Zhuge martial artist standing guard let out a short laugh at the young medical apprentice’s innocent remark. Boredom had led him to bother a child who’d learned nothing but medicine, and now he felt a little guilty.

[P147]
“He is. You’ll understand someday.”

[P148]
“Hmm. Will I?”

[P149]
“If you’re not involved in Murim, you might not know. Anyway, is his training over for today?”

[P150]
Mungyeong tilted his head as though he knew nothing.

[P151]
“No. He said no one should come near him for the next two shichen.”

[P152]
“Understood. We can’t interrupt Great Hero Jin’s training. I’ll tell the guards on the next shift.”

[P153]
“Thank you. Take care.”

[P154]
Mungyeong bowed politely and was about to leave when the martial artist spoke again.

[P155]
“My, his training must be rougher than I thought.”

[P156]
“Sorry?”

[P157]
“The blood on your sleeve. Was Great Hero Jin badly hurt?”

[P158]
The guard’s follow-up question never reached Mungyeong. He looked down at the bloodstain on his sleeve and murmured, “The basics…?”

[P159]
“Hmm?”

[P160]
“Oh, it’s nothing. Young Master Jin is fine, so don’t worry.”

[P161]
“Ah. Good. All right.”

[P162]
Mungyeong walked away, leaving the uneasy-looking guard behind.

[P163]
Several familiar faces greeted him as he passed, but the young medical apprentice had only one person on his mind.

[P164]
*Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung…*

[P165]
He’d thought it couldn’t happen. Yet the boy really had dodged that final sword stroke.

[P166]
The results of the past several days of testing, and of today, had exceeded Mungyeong’s expectations. No, they had exceeded anything he’d imagined.

[P167]
*So this can happen.*

[P168]
Everything he’d told Jin Taekyung was true.

[P169]
He had once taught people he could fairly call Disciples, and all of them had mastered the “basics.”

[P170]
But there was one thing he hadn’t mentioned: how long that had taken.

[P171]
*The fastest of them took a little over a year, if I remember right.*

[P172]
Jin Taekyung had done it in only seven days and nights.

[P173]
No one else came close.

[P174]
Mungyeong didn’t know whether it was because of the boy’s Heavenly Martial Physique or because he was a Supreme Peak master. Whatever the reason, there was something special about Jin Taekyung himself.

[P175]
“Even so… I never expected this much.”

[P176]
He murmured too softly for anyone to hear and rolled up his sleeve.

[P177]
The skin had been cut by something sharp, and beads of blood had formed along the wound. Looking at it, Mungyeong had a sudden thought.

[P178]
*Now I understand how the Fire King feels.*

[P179]
But Mungyeong didn’t realize a faint smile had appeared on his face.

[P180]
[^1]: Teacher’s Day is a Korean holiday observed on May 15 to honor teachers.

[P181]
[^2]: *Salcheonmun* is the name of the now-vanished assassin sect; it literally means “Slaughter Heaven Sect.”

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

After that outburst, Mungyeong returned to his usual calm, dry tone as though nothing had happened.

[P58]
“The basics are just that: the basics. There have been plenty of others like you.”

[P59]
*Others like me?*

[P60]
I ventured a question.

[P61]
“Do you have other Disciples?”

[P62]
“Of course. You met one in Sichuan.”

[P63]
“Other than Old Man Dong. You know what I mean. Don’t change the subject.”

[P64]
“……”

[P65]
Silence was as good as an admission. The thought of the Slaughter Saint’s hidden Disciples made me curious.

[P66]
“Who? Who are they? Do you still keep in touch? Do you all get together for a meal on Teacher’s Day[^1]?”

[P67]
“I have no reason to tell you. And what the hell is Teacher’s Day?”

[P68]
“You’re awfully difficult.”

[P69]
“…You grow more insolent by the day. Do you have five lives or something?”

[P70]
“Considering I’ve died and come back twelve times, I’d say I have about thirteen. So you’re really not going to tell me?”

[P71]
Mungyeong stared at me, then spoke abruptly.

[P72]
“I’ll tell you. On one condition.”

[P73]
A condition from the Slaughter Saint. I answered with complete confidence.

[P74]
“It’s about time to eat. I’ll be going now.”

[P75]
“I distinctly remember you eating before you came.”

[P76]
“I eat five meals a day.”

[P77]
“Stay and hear the condition. You seemed quite curious.”

[P78]
“Everyone has a life of their own and secrets they’d rather keep. Who am I to pry? Anyway, I’ll be off.”

[P79]
“Stop right there if you want to keep your head.”

[P80]
“……”

[P81]
*Fuck. I shouldn’t have asked.*

[P82]
My stomach knotted with panic as I turned back around. Fine. Since I was stuck here, I might as well hear the story.

[P83]
“So you really have other Disciples?”

[P84]
“Not Disciples. But I did teach several people.”

[P85]
“That sounds like you’re saying they’re gone.”

[P86]
“It’s been a very long time. They couldn’t possibly still be alive.”

[P87]
“Were they, by any chance, in the same line of work as…?”

[P88]
“They were assassins. They belonged to Salcheonmun with me.”[^2]

[P89]
*Salcheonmun.* The name alone sounded bloody.

[P90]
*So he belonged to a sect, too.*

[P91]
It made sense. Mungyeong hadn’t been born an assassin.

[P92]
*Still, a sect the Slaughter Saint belonged to should be fairly well known.*

[P93]
But no matter how thoroughly I searched my memory, the name Salcheonmun meant nothing to me.

[P94]
As if he’d read my mind, Mungyeong spoke.

[P95]
“No use trying to remember it. The sect vanished long ago.”

[P96]
There was only one way for a sect to vanish. Watching his expression, I carefully said one word.

[P97]
“Annihilated?”

[P98]
“Yes.”

[P99]
“How did that happen? Wait, weren’t you the Sect Leader?”

[P100]
“They chose the wrong path and paid the price. That’s all I’ll say.”

[P101]
Mungyeong rose. At some point, a short sword had appeared in his hand, its keen edge gleaming blue.

[P102]
“Now it’s time for you to pay.”

[P103]
“Excuse me?”

[P104]
“Dodge one sword stroke. That’s the condition.”

[P105]
Most people would think, *How the hell am I supposed to dodge that?* But I had a decent shot.

[P106]
I’d lasted half an hour against the Slaughter Saint while doing a lousy imitation of an assassin. Surely I could dodge one stroke.

[P107]
“If I do, will you tell me more later?”

[P108]
“Of course.”

[P109]
“Fine. I can do that.”

[P110]
Mungyeong added, “Close your eyes.”

[P111]
“Fuck. Are you kidding me?”

[P112]
“Then you’ll die. Not for the thirteenth time, but for the first and last.”

[P113]
Before he’d finished speaking, Mungyeong’s sleeve fluttered.

[P114]
By now, I was used to his attacks. I instinctively turned my head, but what came flying toward me wasn’t a hidden weapon. It was something else.

[P115]
*That’s…*

[P116]
A powder so fine I could barely make it out even when I strained my eyes to their limit.

[P117]
It rode the wind blowing toward me. The instant the powder touched the air—

[P118]
Whoosh!

[P119]
Darkness swallowed the world.

[P120]
No. That wasn’t right.

[P121]
The darkness hadn’t swallowed the world. It had swallowed me.

[P122]
Beep.

[P123]
> **System**
>
> You have been poisoned by **Blindness Powder**!
>
> You temporarily lose your eyesight!
>
> Rapid **Detoxification** is required! If Detoxification is delayed too long, permanent damage may occur!

[P124]
Every hair on my body stood on end as the System alert sounded in my ears.

[P125]
Blindness Powder? The poison itself didn’t matter. I was still wearing the Myriad-Poison Ring.

[P126]
The problem was that Mungyeong’s sword was coming through the darkness far faster than the ring could detoxify the Blindness Powder.

[P127]
Ssshhk.

[P128]
I couldn’t see a thing. But I could feel it clearly.

[P129]
In a world moving so slowly it felt as though someone had pressed pause, a killing sword approached, erasing the wind in its path.

[P130]
*This is…*

[P131]
A move from the greatest assassin of all time.

[P132]
I felt a killing intent unlike anything I’d ever encountered—so stealthy and chilling that I shuddered.

[P133]
I stared blankly into the darkness.

[P134]
And in that suffocating space where I could see nothing, I felt every sense I had awaken.

[P135]
Slash!

[P136]
* * *

[P137]
Wudang, the Zhuge Clan, and the Beggars’ Sect.

[P138]
They had chosen only trustworthy elites to preserve secrecy, but no one could ignore either the standing or the number of those gathered.

[P139]
Among the hundreds of martial artists from those renowned sects, a young medical apprentice was bound to stand out wherever he went.

[P140]
“Oh, it’s you. Just coming out?”

[P141]
“I’ve just been to see Young Master Jin.”

[P142]
“You seem to visit him more often these days.”

[P143]
“Yes. His training has been so rough lately that he keeps getting hurt.”

[P144]
“Good heavens. Great Hero Jin really is remarkable. He’s younger than my son, but he isn’t content with his current realm. He just keeps working…”

[P145]
“He must be an incredible master. I don’t know much about Murim myself.”

[P146]
The Zhuge martial artist standing guard let out a short laugh at the young medical apprentice’s innocent remark. Boredom had led him to bother a child who’d learned nothing but medicine, and now he felt a little guilty.

[P147]
“He is. You’ll understand someday.”

[P148]
“Hmm. Will I?”

[P149]
“If you’re not involved in Murim, you might not know. Anyway, is his training over for today?”

[P150]
Mungyeong tilted his head as though he knew nothing.

[P151]
“No. He said no one should come near him for the next two shichen.”

[P152]
“Understood. We can’t interrupt Great Hero Jin’s training. I’ll tell the guards on the next shift.”

[P153]
“Thank you. Take care.”

[P154]
Mungyeong bowed politely and was about to leave when the martial artist spoke again.

[P155]
“My, his training must be rougher than I thought.”

[P156]
“Sorry?”

[P157]
“The blood on your sleeve. Was Great Hero Jin badly hurt?”

[P158]
The guard’s follow-up question never reached Mungyeong. He looked down at the bloodstain on his sleeve and murmured, “The basics…?”

[P159]
“Hmm?”

[P160]
“Oh, it’s nothing. Young Master Jin is fine, so don’t worry.”

[P161]
“Ah. Good. All right.”

[P162]
Mungyeong walked away, leaving the uneasy-looking guard behind.

[P163]
Several familiar faces greeted him as he passed, but the young medical apprentice had only one person on his mind.

[P164]
*Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung…*

[P165]
He’d thought it couldn’t happen. Yet the boy really had dodged that final sword stroke.

[P166]
The results of the past several days of testing, and of today, had exceeded Mungyeong’s expectations. No, they had exceeded anything he’d imagined.

[P167]
*So this can happen.*

[P168]
Everything he’d told Jin Taekyung was true.

[P169]
He had once taught people he could fairly call Disciples, and all of them had mastered the “basics.”

[P170]
But there was one thing he hadn’t mentioned: how long that had taken.

[P171]
*The fastest of them took a little over a year, if I remember right.*

[P172]
Jin Taekyung had done it in only seven days and nights.

[P173]
No one else came close.

[P174]
Mungyeong didn’t know whether it was because of the boy’s Heavenly Martial Physique or because he was a Supreme Peak master. Whatever the reason, there was something special about Jin Taekyung himself.

[P175]
“Even so… I never expected this much.”

[P176]
He murmured too softly for anyone to hear and rolled up his sleeve.

[P177]
The skin had been cut by something sharp, and beads of blood had formed along the wound. Looking at it, Mungyeong had a sudden thought.

[P178]
*Now I understand how the Fire King feels.*

[P179]
But Mungyeong didn’t realize a faint smile had appeared on his face.

[P180]
[^1]: Teacher’s Day is a Korean holiday observed on May 15 to honor teachers.

[P181]
[^2]: *Salcheonmun* is the name of the now-vanished assassin sect; it literally means “Slaughter Heaven Sect.”

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
